raw_case_text:
An 88-year-old woman visited our emergency department due to hemoptysis. She had hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dementia due to cerebral infarction. She also had interstitial pneumonia and had been followed up at our hospital but had voluntarily interrupted treatment.
At the time of this admission, her vital signs were normal, and fine crackles were heard from bilateral lower lungs. White blood cells count was increased (19,140 /microL) and serum level of C-reactive protein was slightly increased (3.71 mg/dL). Her hemoglobin level was 8.0 g/dl, hematocrit was 23.1 %, Mean Corpuscular Volume was 80.5 fL, platelet count was 290,000 /microL. Antinuclear antibody, perinuclear-antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA) and C-ANCA were all negative. The result of Interferon-Gamma Release Assay was indeterminate. Chest radiography (Figure 1(Fig. 1)) showed bilateral reticular shadows but no finding of cavity lesions. Contrast-enhanced chest CT showed a honeycomb lung in the right lower lung field and infiltrative shadow and ground glass shadow in the left lower lung field (Figure 2A(Fig. 2)). A contrast-enhancing aneurysm was seen within the infiltrative shadow in the left lower lung, but no obvious cavitary lesion was seen (Figure 2B-D(Fig. 2)).
We thought the patient's hemoptysis was caused by an aneurysm in the lower left lung field. We performed angiography (Figure 3(Fig. 3)) and successfully performed endovascular coil embolization of an aneurysm in the pulmonary artery. After these treatments, sputum screening tested positive for acid-fast bacillus. She was diagnosed with pulmonary TB based on the result of polymerase chain reaction positive for mycobacterium TB. She was treated with isoniazid (INH), rifampicin (RFP), and ethambutol (EB) without pyrazinamide (PZA) due to problems with liver function. No recurrence of hemoptysis was observed after successfully treating pulmonary TB.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 88-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with hemoptysis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: An 88-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with acute hemoptysis. She had a known history of interstitial pneumonia previously managed at the hospital, but had voluntarily discontinued her treatment.
subjective.past_medical_history: Hypertension, diabetes mellitus, vascular dementia secondary to cerebral infarction, and interstitial pneumonia (treatment voluntarily discontinued). Prior TB history, travel, and animal/TB contacts not documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports hemoptysis; denies fever, chest pain, dyspnea, chills, hematemesis, or melena. Home medications and drug allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs within normal limits. Chest auscultation: fine crackles audible over bilateral lower lung fields. Cardiovascular, abdominal, and extremity examinations unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: WBC: 19,140/microL; CRP: 3.71 mg/dL; Hemoglobin: 8.0 g/dL; Hematocrit: 23.1%; MCV: 80.5 fL; Platelets: 290,000/microL; ANA, p-ANCA, and c-ANCA: all negative; Interferon-Gamma Release Assay (IGRA): indeterminate. Chest radiography: bilateral reticular opacities without evident cavitary lesions.
objective.advanced_workup: Contrast-enhanced chest CT: honeycomb changes in right lower lung field, infiltrative shadow and ground-glass opacities in left lower lung field, and a contrast-enhancing aneurysm within the infiltrative shadow in left lower lung without obvious cavitary lesions. Angiography: confirmed a left pulmonary artery branch aneurysm.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Pulmonary tuberculosis presenting with a pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm (Rasmussen's-type aneurysm) and hemoptysis, superimposed on chronic interstitial pneumonia.
Confirmation: Sputum screening was positive for acid-fast bacilli (AFB), and sputum polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
Differentials ruled out: ANCA-associated vasculitis and systemic autoimmune diseases (p-ANCA, c-ANCA, ANA negative), non-tuberculous mycobacterial infection.
Treatment & Outcome: Urgent endovascular coil embolization of the left pulmonary artery aneurysm was successfully performed via angiography, arresting hemoptysis. Following confirmation of tuberculosis, antituberculous therapy was started with isoniazid (INH), rifampicin (RFP), and ethambutol (EB); pyrazinamide (PZA) was omitted due to baseline hepatic dysfunction. Complete resolution of pulmonary tuberculosis was achieved with no recurrence of hemoptysis.
